this is for an Xbox controller since I've been told a lot of the tutorial is still in japanese

  • left analog stick is movement and right analog stick is camera

  • R2 trigger - dodge or block the way you dodge is different by class and weapon

  • A button - jump

  • B button - pick up items access things

  • so there are two boxes on the bottom middle part of your screen these access 4 attacks set to your current weapon X button for your basic attack and combos Y button for your 1st set technique or Photon art and then while holding the R1 bumper X and Y now access two other techniques

  • now there's also a list of numbered icons around them this is your sub palette use left and right on the cursor pad to switch between them and L2 trigger to use the one you have selected

  • L1 bumper to lock on to a specific enemy but the auto lock on is usually easier

  • up and down on the cursor pad switch between weapons if you have more than one set up

/u/caelumsixsmith also said (I'll make all this into one list with the rest later I've been running around NYC all day); It's all customizable and I highly recommend players check out the options whether they play with controller or kb/m. That's on the gear icon on the menu, then settings and under "control options" (or something like that) you'll find everything from kb/m, to controller, to controller calibration, to keyboard shortcuts (such as Lobby Actions)... It's very detailed. It's interesting to check that out for people who play with a controller and change constantly between third person and TPS cameras.

Subpalettes also have books. You can change books by selecting the weapon palette and (based on controller commands) press D-pad left or right to change to the subpalette selection. Quite handy for tech users!

I leave direct chat on since I, too, use a controller -- so there's no need to hit Enter before typing.

I set auto-run for the left stick's click and the TPS camera for the right stick's click. My TPS camera has commands on the triggers and bumpers instead of the face buttons as it's easier to attack and use PA/techs whilst moving the camera.

Oh, and don't forget Select/mouse wheel! That's a very important sub-menu with things like NPC partner commands (from there you should set them to sync PB instead of using it freely and the option in Japanese is to set them to offensive or supportive modes), cameras to take pictures, lobby mini map and instant teleportation to My Room and Team Room, among other things.

I had an issue with the PS4's dualshock 4 controller not working properly with the DS4windows application and found a solution after many hours of troubleshooting. Ill just cut and paste my forum post below describing the issue and how I solved it:

Thanks for the program, its awesome. I have an issue. Whenever I choose "Hide DS4" option, the "wireless controller" still shows up under devices and printers. Im running the latest version of the application on windows 8.1. My problem is that a game im trying to play (phantasy star online 2) is seeing the "wireless controller" dinput device and using that automatically, instead of the xinput device (dark souls 1 also does this). Any reason why the "hide ds4" option isnt working for me? anything I should try?

I actually solved this issue. So what im GUESSING was happening was PSO2 was picking up BOTH the default stick input from the dinput device AND the input from ds4windows. I went into ds4windows and DISABLED the right stick (the one that was having all the issues) and left all four directions unbound and BAM everything started working properly.

Im just writing this here in case anyone else is trying to use ds4windows and phantasy star online 2 together. Its not an issue with analog triggers or anything like that. Just leave the L stick and L2/R2 bound correctly and unbind the right stick all together. Check hide DS4 controller in the settings and your good to go! You have to restart PSO2 for it to pick up on the new configuration, and then go through the controller setup wizard which should pick everything up correctly.
